chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the sun declines, the time of the two salats has entered, except that this one (Zuhr) is before this one (Asr).

And Sa'd reported, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, altogether from al-Qasim and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim — similar to it, and in it: 'The time of al-Zuhr and al-Asr enters together.' And he added: 'Then you are in the time belonging to both of them together, until the sun sets.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: The two salats — specifically Zuhr and Asr prayers
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun's zawal (decline from zenith) — the precise moment marking the sun's passage of the midday meridian, triggering prayer times
key_terms.وَقْتُ الظُّهْرِ وَالْعَصْرِ: The time of Zuhr and Asr — referring to the combined window of validity for both prayers

ai.seo_question: When do the times of Zuhr and Asr prayers begin according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the ruling that when the sun declines from its zenith (zawal), the prayer times for both Zuhr (noon prayer) and Asr (afternoon prayer) simultaneously become valid — with Zuhr taking precedence over Asr. A corroborating report through a parallel chain adds that one remains in the combined time window for both prayers until sunset. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential position that Zuhr and Asr share a combined time period, differing from some Sunni schools that require specific intervals between them.
